'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Togoga airstrike]]
***Doctors and medical workers in the [[Tigray Region]] say that more than 80 civilians have been killed and dozens more have been injured in an [[airstrike]] on a busy market in the village of [[Togoga]]. [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Ethiopian soldiers]] have reportedly prevented a convoy of [[ambulance]]s from reaching the village. [https://apnews.com/article/ap-top-news-kenya-africa-ethiopia-424851651a0e02c21df71c86d9b70ec2 (AP)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Three people are killed and 13 others injured during an explosion near the residence of [[Hafiz Saeed|Hafiz Muhammad Saeed]], the founder of the Islamist terrorist group [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]], in [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]]. Saeed's residence is suspected to be the attack's target. Saeed is serving is serving an 11-year prison sentence. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/23/pakistan-blast-hafiz-saeed-lahore-residence (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Suspected [[Taliban]] [[insurgent]]s fire a rocket into a hospital in [[Kunar Province|Kunar]], destroying [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s and setting the hospital on fire. Taliban spokesman [[Zabiullah Mujahid]] denies responsibility for the attack as the group [[Taliban insurgency|gains more territory]] on [[Afghanistan-Tajikistan border|the border]] with [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-hospital-burns-after-attack-taliban-seize-border-post-north-2021-06-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**The [[Southern African Development Community]] agrees to deploy a "standby force" to northern [[Mozambique]] to contain the growing [[Islamism|Islamist]] insurgency in [[Cabo Delgado Province|the area]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/23/southern-african-nations-agree-to-deploy-forces-to-mozambique (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] surpasses 30 million cases of [[COVID-19]], becoming the second country to do so after the [[United States]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/indias-new-covid-19-cases-and-deaths-rise-to-50-848-and-1-358-tally-tops-30-million-101624415638420.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 15,308 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.03 million. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5617349/dki-jabar-jateng-tertinggi-ini-sebaran-15308-kasus-baru-covid-19-ri-23-juni (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://m.akipress.com/news:659708:Mongolia_s_coronavirus_count_passes_100,000_cases/ (AKI Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 51 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,744. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2137039/record-51-covid-deaths-3-174-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****New restrictions are imposed in [[Sydney]] and surrounding towns as the number of COVID-19 cases increases. Household visits are limited to five people, capacity quotas are introduced at businesses and [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|masks are made mandatory]] in all non-residential indoor settings. The other states and territories of [[Australia]], as well as [[New Zealand]], close their borders with [[New South Wales]]. [https://www.nsw.gov.au/media-releases/new-covid-19-restrictions-for-greater-sydney-23-june-2021 (NSW Government)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 279 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total to 2,549. The [[Ministry of Health (Fiji)|Ministry of Health]] also reports four deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445384/covid-infections-in-fiji-soar-four-deaths-reported (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
***[[Ukraine]] reports its first two cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] in a woman and a teenager who travelled from [[Russia]]. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/delta-most-dangerous-coronavirus-variant-yet-detected-in-ukraine.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area]]
*****[[San Francisco]] will require all 35,000 of their city employees to take the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/24/world/san-francisco-vaccine-mandate.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]]
****[[Clallam County, Washington| Clallam County]] in [[Washington (state)|Washington]] reports their first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Gamma variant|Lineage P.1 Gamma variant]] in an unvaccinated resident who traveled out of the state. [https://www.peninsuladailynews.com/news/gamma-variant-of-covid-19-discovered-in-clallam-county/ (''Peninsula Daily News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] reports 115,228 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record. [https://www.rte.ie/news/coronavirus/2021/0624/1231026-world-virus/ (RTE)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United Kingdom relations]]
**Russia's [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Defence Ministry]] says that a [[Russian Navy]] patrol ship fired shots and a [[Sukhoi Su-24|Su-24]] attack aircraft dropped bombs in the pathway of the [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Royal Navy]] destroyer {{HMS|Defender|D36|6}} after it reportedly entered Russian-claimed territorial waters near [[Crimea]] in the [[Black Sea]]. The UK [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|MOD]] said that this was part of a Russian military exercise in the vicinity and rejected Russia's account of the incident denying that any shots or bombs had been directed at the British ship. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-57583363 (BBC News)]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of Commerce|U.S. Department of Commerce]] places sanctions on five [[China|Chinese]] companies, some of them major producers of [[solar panel]] parts, for using forced [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] labor. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/23/us-sanctions-chinese-solar-firms-for-uighur-human-rights-abuses (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[United Nations]] votes 184-2 on a resolution ending the [[embargo]] on [[Cuba]], with the [[United States]] and [[Israel]] being the lone no votes. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-continues-vote-against-un-call-end-cuba-embargo-2021-06-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**An [[Indiana]] woman is sentenced to three years [[probation]] for her role in the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|attack]] on the [[United States Capitol]], making her the first person to be sentenced in the riot. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/im-ashamed-woman-breached-capitol-receives-probation-1st/story?id=78445859 (ABC News)]
**Graydon Young pleads guilty to [[conspiracy (criminal)|conspiracy]] charges for his role in the Capitol [[riot]], making him the first member of the [[Oath Keepers]] to do so. [https://www.npr.org/2021/06/23/1009597270/first-guilty-plea-january-6-oath-keepers-conspiracy-case (NPR)]
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The nine [[Catalan separatist]]s [[pardon]]ed on Tuesday leave prison after their pardons were ratified by [[Monarchy of Spain|King]] [[Felipe VI]] and after the [[Supreme Court of Spain|Supreme Court]] set their imminent release. [https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20210623/lideres-del-proces-indultados-salen-prision-arropados-independentismo/2108680.shtml (RTVE)]
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**The pro-[[democracy]] newspaper ''[[Apple Daily]]'' announces that its final edition will be released on Thursday and that it will later cease activities after five top executives were arrested under the national security law and the newspaper's assets were frozen. ''Apple Daily'' founder [[Jimmy Lai]] is already imprisoned and awaits trial, along with 46 others, on subversion charges. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/23/media/apple-daily-closure-intl-hnk-dst/index.html (CNN)]
*[[LGBT rights in Poland]]
**Polish education minister [[Przemysław Czarnek]] accuses the [[LGBT community]] of "insulting public morality" for a march held on Saturday in support of [[LGBT rights|rights for the community]]. The opposition condemns Czarnek's comments as "language of hate". [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-education-minister-says-lgbt-march-insult-public-morality-2021-06-23/ (Reuters)]
*American businessman [[John McAfee]] is found dead in his [[Barcelona]] prison cell, believed to be caused by [[suicide]] after the [[Audiencia Nacional|Spanish High Court]] authorized an [[extradition]] request for [[tax evasion]] earlier in the day. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/john-mcafee-found-dead-prison-after-spanish-court-allows-extradition-2021-06-23/ (Reuters)] 
*The [[Cowessess First Nation]] and the [[Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations]] announce the discovery of hundreds of unmarked graves at the site of the former [[Marieval Indian Residential School]] in [[Saskatchewan]], Canada. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/cowessess-graves-unmarked-residential-school-marieval-1.6077797 (CBC News)]
